nar.text: It was not a particularly hot day and an overcast sky suggested that it was going to rain.
Ten cars take the flying start: six Bugattis, three Delages and Segrave's 4-litre Sunbeam.
Benoist's Delage leads off, but within a few hundred metres the Sunbeam is in front; Segrave completes lap one 200 metres ahead of Benoist.
On lap two Segrave was still in first place followed by Benoist who had closed up with a lap of 7m57.8s at 130.405 km/h average, then Wagner, Morel and Costantini
Goux stops to replace plugs in 2m09s and restarts last.
De Buck skids into the palisade at Urnieta and twists a steering rod.
After the third lap the order was Segrave, Morel who had passed Wagner, Costantini and Benoist who was heading for the pits, Minoia, Williams, Ferry and Goux.
Benoist spends nine minutes in the pits on the ignition, changing eight plugs. Heavy rain begins.
Up to the fourth lap the race average was 130 km/h but then strong rain began and the average speed dropped momentarily to 99 km/h.
Morel passes Segrave for the lead; Wagner and Costantini follow closely.
Benoist returns to the pits to retire.
Goux was experiencing brake problems which were later corrected.
Segrave is missing: the Sunbeam's front axle broke at 145 km/h at kilometre 6. He is unhurt.
Morel retires; Wagner's Delage leads from Costantini, Williams and Minoia.
It continued drizzling and the average speed remained low because the roads were slippery.
Goux passes Ferry and Minoia for fourth; Wagner leads Costantini by 20 seconds.
After 11 laps Wagner was still in the lead, but Costantini in second place started pushing harder while Goux passed Williams and gained third place.
On lap 12, Wagner and Costantini both managed to lap Ferry and Minoia who were in the last places.
Costantini passes Wagner's Delage for the lead, to an ovation.
The rain stops; Costantini sets a lap record of 7m53.8s, with Wagner 18 seconds behind.
Ferry stops for 3m50s to refuel and hands over to Ivanowsky.
On lap 16 Costantini continued to increase his pace beating the lap record again with a time of 7m44.8s the equivalent of 134.50 km/h per hour.
Wagner stops for two minutes to add water and Benoist takes over.
Costantini makes his first stop: fuel in 1m19s, to an ovation from the grandstand.
After 20 laps Costantini leads Benoist, in Wagner's Delage, by seven minutes; Goux is third, a lap down.
Benoist, in Wagner's Delage, loses 8m47s changing plugs; Costantini stops briefly to replace a hood strap.
It rained again and the speed of most drivers slowed as the race average dropped on lap 22 to 118 km/h.
Costantini leads Benoist, in Wagner's Delage, by 7m55s.
On lap 27, Costantini lapped Benoist in Wagner's Delage, continuing his magnificent drive.
Williams pits and, after close examination, retires: valves, punctures, plugs and fatigue.
On lap 30 Costantini had increased his advantage over Benoist to 10m13s, already one lap behind.
Goux breaks a lever but keeps going fast.
Goux and Benoist make their last fuel stops; Goux, now second, takes 1m59s. Costantini leads Goux by 14m16s.
Costantini wins; Goux and Benoist, in Wagner's Delage, are a lap behind, Minoia two.
Ivanowsky in Ferry's Bugatti, which suffered from preparation deficiencies, was stopped by the officials with only 33 laps completed.
